items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: As a matter of fact I have a drum that Bill made for me

ctx.x: As a matter of fact I have a drum that Bill made for me, you know, and there weren’t that many drummers on the scene in LA at that time. Young guys, you know. And it was cool. And mainly, you know, like I said I was self-taught, just dug everything I could. You know, I would always try something.

Now you talked about when you were growing up and we were talking even before we began running the tape about how, you know, you basically were poor but it just meant you didn’t have -- you weren’t materially wealthy in that regard but, you know, there was a real sense of community. Now were you born and raised in the same community? Did you move around at all?
